solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Novelist needs study with minimal source of heat

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
a radiator cut short is RAD, so a minimal heater

explanation.surface: A writer needs a study warmed only slightly to work in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minimal' shortens radiator to its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Conrad wrote Heart of Darkness and Lord Jim, so he is a novelist.

clue.text: Cold month has fifty leaving holiday island

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: the Roman numeral for fifty goes out of the month

parts.note: April is a month
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A chilly month means fifty holidaymakers depart from the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an Italian island in the Bay of Naples, a popular resort.

clue.text: Telescope unmanageable without its bottom component

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the last letter, which is dropped

parts.note: refractory means stubborn and hard to manage

explanation.surface: A telescope becomes awkward to handle when its base part is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom component' is the last letter, Y, in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A refractor is a telescope that uses lenses to bend light.

clue.text: Doctor faced with hospital being demolished — terrible

indicators.note: the hospital letter is knocked out of the word

parts.note: to head something is to face or front it
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A doctor confronting the closure of his hospital finds it awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faced' gives HEADED, and 'being demolished' removes the H.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreaded is feared greatly, so awful in prospect.

clue.text: Bird half-hidden by brown plant

indicators.note: only half of the bird's name shows, its first three letters, the rest being hidden

parts.note: the cuckoo is a bird
umber is a brown earth pigment, and the colour

explanation.surface: A bird is half-concealed by a brown plant it sits in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hidden' suggests the bird lurks in the plant, but it means only half the bird's name is shown.
explanation.definitionFit: The cucumber is a trailing vine grown for its long green fruit.

clue.text: Formality of style that could make connoisseur seem silly

indicators.note: the words are made silly, jumbled out of their sensible order

explanation.surface: Pomp of manner that could make an expert look foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceremoniousness is a manner full of ritual and formal politeness.

clue.text: It's unlike a nude chap to get embarrassed

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a man or chap
an embarrassed face goes red

explanation.surface: A naked man would hardly blush, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A nude wears nothing, whereas someone clothed has a garment on.

clue.text: Where one may leave for travel — kiss most important

definitions.text: Where one may leave for travel

parts.note: buss is an old word for a kiss
top means foremost, most important

explanation.surface: A farewell kiss before a trip matters most.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers wait at a bus stop to board and leave.

clue.text: Gentle sounds made by reddish-brown fish

parts.note: rust is a reddish-brown colour
the ling is a long fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Soft noises made by coppery fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustle is a soft crackling noise, like leaves or paper moving.

clue.text: Bunk two fellows installed in tall building

indicators.note: the two fellows are placed inside the word for the building

parts.note: a pile is a large tall building
F is the abbreviation for fellow, so two of them give FF

explanation.surface: Nonsense: two blokes put into a tower block.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunk, short for bunkum, is nonsense, as is piffle.

clue.text: Backs Scripture portions in school lessons?

parts.note: RE is religious education, a subject taught in British schools
the Bible is divided into chapters and verses

explanation.surface: Bible verses are studied during religious lessons at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backs' is a verb: to back a car is to reverse it.
explanation.definitionFit: To back is to move backwards, which is what one reverses means.

clue.text: This person's binding religious books by unorthodox dean together

indicators.note: the contraction wraps round the books and the reworked dean, as a cover binds pages

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself: this person is = I'M
NT is the New Testament

indicators.note: an unorthodox dean has his letters out of the usual order

explanation.surface: A writer says he is binding holy books beside a heretical dean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person's' is the setter speaking of himself, a common convention; 'unorthodox' rearranges the dean's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Working in tandem means operating jointly, side by side.

clue.text: Payment concerning mum maybe, but not dad

indicators.note: the father's word is to be left out of the adjective

parts.note: parental means relating to a parent, such as mum
pa is an informal word for dad

explanation.surface: A payment involving mother, though father is left out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rental is the sum paid to hire or lease something.

clue.text: Builder has engraved amphibian, not a huge beast

indicators.note: a mason carves into stone, so the builder's word takes another inside it

parts.note: a mason builds in stone

indicators.note: the a of the clue is dropped from the creature's name

parts.note: a toad is an amphibian

explanation.surface: A stonemason has carved a toad, though not a giant creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a' reads as a contrast in the surface but removes the letter A from the amphibian.
explanation.definitionFit: The mastodon was a huge extinct elephant-like mammal.

clue.text: Form of entertainment with which American children may enthral one in street

indicators.note: the whole group sits inside the street's name

parts.note: the Mall is a famous London street, so mall stands for street

indicators.note: the American and the children hold the one between them, as if captivating it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: American kids might enthrall a passer-by with street performance.
explanation.walkthrough: THE MALL is a London street leading to Buckingham Palace. US and CH hold I, then MALL holds the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Music hall was British variety theatre of songs, comedy and acts.

clue.text: Confined water? Then enclosure becomes wet

parts.note: a dam holds back water, and the water held is also called a dam
a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: Water held back, and then an animal pen turns soggy.
explanation.definitionFit: To dampen something is to make it slightly moist.

clue.text: Victorian city suffering mob rule with one leader deposed

indicators.note: the letters suffer, pushed out of shape into a new order
the first letter of one is removed, as a leader is ousted

explanation.surface: A nineteenth-century town endures mob rule and has its single chief ousted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victorian' means in the Australian state of Victoria, not of the 1800s. 'leader deposed' turns ONE into NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Melbourne is the capital of the state of Victoria in Australia.

clue.text: Ruler didn't stand criticism

parts.note: one who sat stayed seated rather than standing
a rap is a rebuke, as in a rap on the knuckles

explanation.surface: A ruler would not put up with criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'didn't stand' looks like tolerating; it means remained seated.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial governor in ancient Persia, hence any petty ruler.

clue.text: Such could arrange men to be in formal attire

definitions.text: Such could arrange men to be in formal attire

indicators.note: the men are placed inside the word for the formal dress

parts.note: tails are a formal tailcoat
OR means other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Such people could see to it that men turn out in evening dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothiers make and fit suits, so they dress men in formal wear.

clue.text: Spend time making transition

parts.note: to pass time is to spend it
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Using up time while moving from one state to another.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a movement or change from one place or state to another.

clue.text: What's cut Sol's supply? Put in answer: eclipse

indicators.note: the letter for answer is placed inside the rearranged letters
supply read as supple-ly, in a flexible way, bends the letters of cut and Sol's into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A riddle: what cuts off the Sun's supply? The reply is an eclipse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' reads as a noun but is the adverb from supple, rearranging the letters to OUTCLSS before the A goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse a rival is to surpass them so far they are overshadowed.

clue.text: Like some junctions bound to restrict cars and such ultimately

indicators.note: the bound word holds the other letters in, restricting them

parts.note: taped means bound up with tape

indicators.note: the last letter of each of the two words is taken

explanation.surface: Junctions are bound to limit traffic in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes S and H, the ends of 'cars' and 'such'; 'bound to' looks like certain to.
explanation.definitionFit: Where one road meets another at a right angle without crossing, the layout forms a capital T.

clue.text: Trousers with feature made for a really big customer

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

parts.words: made for a really big customer
parts.note: OS stands for outsize, the label on clothes for very large people

explanation.surface: Trousers with a detail tailored for an enormous client.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinos are casual trousers of cotton twill.

clue.text: Rather engaging church glass

indicators.note: the word for rather takes in the church, holding it within

parts.note: sooner means rather, as in I'd sooner not

explanation.surface: A fairly attractive church window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaging' reads as charming but signals one piece holding another.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a tall drinking glass, used for sherry or beer.

clue.text: Quarrel brings any number into devastation

indicators.note: the number letter goes inside the word for devastation

parts.note: ruin is destruction or devastation
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: An argument causes untold destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-in is an argument or clash with someone.

clue.text: Rubbish penned by a model who has defected

indicators.note: the rubbish is enclosed by the following words, as if written in a pen

parts.note: to pose is to model for an artist
tat is shoddy rubbish

explanation.surface: Trash written by a fashion model who has switched sides.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate is someone who has abandoned their religion or cause.

clue.text: Sort of indulgence — what you'd expect with Giovanni?

parts.note: par is the normal or expected level, as in par for the course
Don Giovanni is Mozart's opera, so Don goes with Giovanni

explanation.surface: The setter, Giovanni, asks us to forgive his habits as par for him.
explanation.walkthrough: Giovanni is the setter's own pseudonym, which makes the surface self-mocking.
explanation.definitionFit: In the medieval church a pardon was an indulgence remitting punishment for sin.

clue.text: Tip a smaller amount of money, being half-hearted

parts.note: to list is to lean or tip over, as a ship does
less means a smaller amount

explanation.surface: Leaving a small gratuity shows lack of enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like a gratuity, but it is the verb to lean.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone listless lacks energy and enthusiasm, doing things without spirit.

clue.text: What has Andrews contracted?

definitions.meaning: the name Andrews has the name Drew sitting in it, so what it has is ...
drawn in means pulled together, made smaller

explanation.definitionFit: When something has drawn in it has shrunk or tightened, like days in autumn.
